description: Under the strict Content Security Policy every framework script and style carries the request token, so page scripts, click handlers and page styles work on a full load and after SPA navigation, a static cached page carries the token of its own response, and nothing is blocked

browserSteps.value: fetch(location.href, { cache: 'no-store' }).then((response) => { const policy = response.headers.get('Content-Security-Policy') ?? ''; if (!policy.includes("'strict-dynamic'") || !policy.includes("'nonce-")) { throw new Error('the page is not served under the strict policy: ' + policy); }})
First request: the page script, the runtime and the page style all carry the request token

new Promise((resolve, reject) => { const seen = [...(window.__cspViolations ?? [])]; let observer = null; if (typeof ReportingObserver === 'function') {  observer = new ReportingObserver((reports) => { for (const report of reports) { seen.push(report.body.effectiveDirective + ' ' + report.body.blockedURL); } }, { types: ['csp-violation'], buffered: true });  observer.observe(); } setTimeout(() => {  if (observer) { for (const report of observer.takeRecords()) { seen.push(report.body.effectiveDirective + ' ' + report.body.blockedURL); } observer.disconnect(); }  if (seen.length > 0) { reject(new Error('the Content Security Policy blocked: ' + seen.join(', '))); } else { resolve(true); } }, 300);})
Second request for the same static page gets a new token, so the page must not be a stored copy carrying the first one

SPA navigation: the runtime loads the next page's script, which 'strict-dynamic' allows, and inserts its page style with the page's token
